status_summary: On 2026-01-26 OCR published two notices, effective on publication: one (FR 2026-01434, 91 FR 3207) disavowing or repudiating the 2021 University of Vermont Medical Center letter, three 2021 RFRA foster care exemption letters, the 2021 California Weldon Amendment letter and 2021 COVID-19 vaccine equity guidance, and another (FR 2026-01435, 91 FR 3206) rescinding the 2021-09-17 Church Amendments nondiscrimination guidance; on 2026-01-27 it rescinded its September 2023 retail pharmacy guidance (FR 2026-01550). HHS announced on 2026-01-21 a Notice of Violation to Illinois finding that referral requirements in a state conscience law violate the Weldon and Coats-Snowe Amendments, with no deadline or funding consequence stated, and on 2026-03-19 announced Weldon Amendment investigations of thirteen unnamed states. OCR's organization notice (approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28) lists a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division headed by a Deputy Director, naming the Church, Coats-Snowe and Weldon amendments and ACA sections 1303(b)(4) and 1553, but it does not mention RFRA or list new delegations. Not found in the sources reached: a final RFRA rule, withdrawal of the June 2022 HIPAA guidance, passage of the Conscience Protection Act, or funding terminations tied to conscience findings.

timeline.event: HHS OCR issues a Notice of Violation to Illinois finding that referral requirements in the Illinois Health Care Right of Conscience Act violate the Weldon and Coats-Snowe Amendments, and a nationwide Dear Colleague Letter on federal conscience statutes; no deadline or funding consequence is stated.

OCR publishes a notice rescinding or disavowing four sets of earlier documents under Executive Order 14192 (University of Vermont Medical Center letter, three RFRA foster care letters, California Weldon letter, COVID-19 vaccine equity guidance).
OCR publishes a notice (91 FR 3206) rescinding its 2021-09-17 guidance on nondiscrimination protections under the Church Amendments, effective on publication.

OCR rescinds its September 29, 2023 retail pharmacy civil rights guidance, effective on publication; the abstract says the 2023 guidance had revised a 2022 guidance on reproductive health care access at pharmacies.
HHS modifies OCR's Privacy Act system of records to add records on complaints and reviews involving civil rights, conscience, religious freedom and health information privacy.
HHS announces OCR investigations of thirteen states (not named in the release) over laws alleged to require coverage of abortion contrary to the Weldon Amendment.

Federal Register publishes OCR's organization notice (approved 2026-05-14, effective 2026-06-28) describing a Conscience and Religious Freedom Division that runs OCR's national conscience and religious freedom enforcement program.

title: Restore OCR conscience enforcement and rescind Biden-era conscience and pharmacy guidance
uncertainties: The three rescission notices (FR 2026-01434, 2026-01435, 2026-01550 as previously checked) and the organization notice were read on the Federal Register host, and the HHS fact sheet of 2026-01-21 and the HHS release of 2026-03-19 were read on hhs.gov. The 2026-03-19 release does not name the thirteen states or say when letters were sent; a news report names them and dates the letters 2026-03-18, which was not confirmed on a primary host. Enforcement outcomes after the Illinois Notice of Violation (resolution, funding action), a RFRA rule and OGC memo rescission were not confirmed. The organization notice does not say whether the division was newly established or restored, and it replaced a strategic planning division in OCR's structure. The pharmacy rescission abstract states the 2023 guidance had revised a 2022 guidance; whether the 2022 pharmacy guidance remains posted was not checked. Context, not an action on this objective: a federal court in Texas (Purl v. HHS, N.D. Tex., No. 2:24-cv-00228-Z) vacated most of the separate 2024 HIPAA reproductive health privacy rule on 2025-06-18, and law-firm reports say HHS did not appeal and the Fifth Circuit dismissed the intervenors' appeal in September 2025. That ruling concerns a different instrument from the June 2022 HIPAA guidance the Mandate targets, and the HHS reproductive health HIPAA page still links the guidance on disclosures relating to reproductive health care, so withdrawal of the June 2022 guidance was not found.
